summary.text: Monique Chandler-Waterman is the Democratic and Working Families Party incumbent for Assembly District 58 in Brooklyn. A lifelong Brooklyn resident, she worked in community organizing, local nonprofit work and City Council outreach before winning a May 2022 special election to succeed N. Nick Perry. She was re-elected in 2022 and 2024 and is unopposed on the November 2026 ballot.

paragraphs.text: According to her official biography, she was born January 14, 1981, raised in East Flatbush, and is the daughter of Jamaican and Barbadian immigrants. Ballotpedia lists her birthplace as New York City.
She graduated from Boys and Girls High School, earned a bachelor's degree in business administration from Berkeley College, and received an MBA from Metropolitan College of New York.

Her official biography says she began organizing local block associations in 2005 and in 2008 co-founded a nonprofit providing academic, cultural, mental health and violence-prevention programs to families. Ballotpedia says she founded a day care center and co-founded the nonprofit East Flatbush Village, Inc.

Her official biography lists roles as Civilian Advisor for the NYPD's 67th Precinct, director of community outreach for then-City Council Member Jumaane Williams, and Outreach Director for New York City's Test & Trace Corps during the COVID-19 pandemic.
She won a May 2022 special election to succeed N. Nick Perry in the Assembly, after his appointment as U.S. Ambassador to Jamaica, and was re-elected in the 2022 and 2024 general elections.
For the 2025-2026 session she serves on the Banks, Children and Families, Election Law, Higher Education, Housing, and Mental Health committees.

Her official biography lists her as co-chair of the Anti-Gun Violence Subcommittee of the Black, Puerto Rican, Hispanic and Asian Legislative Caucus and of the Mental Health Subcommittee of the Black Legislative Taskforce, and a participant in the Legislative Women's Caucus.

Honors named in her official biography include the New York City Council's Shirley Chisholm Woman of Distinction Award, the Caribbean Life Impact 40 Under 40 Award and the UFT School Safety Award. It says she lives in East Flatbush with her husband, Eric Waterman, and their four children.
